outcome: Meetings, calling and room devices delivered from one platform with retention and residency options that satisfy regulated buyers.
overview: Collaboration platform decisions are unusual: the technology comparison is narrow and the change-management problem is enormous, because the outcome lands on every desk in the organisation on the same morning. Webex covers meetings, calling and room devices under one platform with retention and residency options that matter to regulated buyers. Redington’s contribution is mostly the unglamorous half — measuring what is genuinely in use today, checking that sites can carry real-time media, and sequencing a rollout that does not strand a department mid-migration.

benefits.text: Meetings, calling and room devices come from one platform rather than three contracts
benefits.limits: Consolidation saves only where the replaced contracts are actually ended, and their renewal dates rarely align

benefits.text: Retention and residency options exist for organisations that cannot accept a default
benefits.limits: Options vary by service component and region and must be confirmed per component rather than assumed platform-wide

benefits.text: Room devices and personal clients share one management and identity model
benefits.limits: Existing room hardware from other vendors may work in a limited mode; the device inventory decides how much is replaced

residency: Data residency and retention options differ per service component; the position is established per component during design and recorded, not asserted platform-wide

notFor.situation: An organisation whose productivity suite already includes a collaboration platform in active use
notFor.why: Running two collaboration platforms splits the organisation and neither reaches full adoption

notFor.situation: A workforce with no meeting rooms and no calling requirement
notFor.why: The consolidation argument depends on covering more than meetings

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco collaboration implementation partner · Duration: 10–16 weeks to a migrated pilot population with a room standard in place
Support model: Vendor subscription and device support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed adoption programme.
1) Baseline — measured tool usage, room inventory, site media readiness and retention obligations
2) Design — room standards, identity integration, retention per content type, population sequence
3) Pilot — one population and a set of rooms migrated with adoption and quality measured
4) Roll out and hand over — remaining populations migrated, legacy contracts exited, operations handed over
deliverables: Media quality at each migrated site meets the threshold agreed after the readiness assessment
Retention is configured per content type against the stated obligations
A room device and a personal client present the same identity and reachability for a user
